calendar.impact: An energy ceasefire is on Ukraine's agenda for the first direct talks since February, against the heaviest refinery strike week of the autumn: six Russian plants struck since Oct 30, Yanos halted, and Saratov hit overnight into Nov 7.
calendar.title: US-hosted Ukraine and Russia talks, Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11)

calendar.impact: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 is released a day late for Veterans Day, at 12:00 p.m. ET. It is the first balance print after the repricing, and distillate at 99.3 million barrels is the line that matters.
calendar.title: EIA weekly petroleum report, 12:00 p.m. ET (delayed for Veterans Day)

calendar.impact: The deadline for December shipper nominations. The registered December judgment call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows the close.
calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close

calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the fourth quarter capacity review setting the baselines for 2027 quotas.
calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework

changes.balance: The premium is repriced and the new level held into the weekend: two recovery days and a flat Friday on an unchanged physical board, with strait transit still below 60 percent of capacity on the ANZ gauge, tanker attacks at a record pace, and a negotiation channel that is live and rejecting drafts. The positioning print changes the week's grading: funds cut the combined Brent and WTI net long by 78,492 contracts in the week to Nov 3, before Wednesday's fall, so the length that fed the flush is largely spent.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled at $98.32 on Friday, up $0.03, and WTI Dec26 settled at $90.83, up $0.31 (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 6), closing a week in which front-month futures fell about 13.2 percent, the biggest weekly percentage loss since 2022, inside a $19 range since Monday. Tehran called Washington's latest reply not convincing, the mediators await an answer on a new proposal, and the president said Friday he will decide soon between a peace deal and destroying what remains of Iran. UKMTO counts at least five vessel incidents since Sunday, close to October's record pace of 35 vessels hit, and an explosion aboard a product tanker on Nov 5 killed one crew member. Brent managed money cut net length by 63,487 contracts to 181,970 in the week ending Nov 3 (ICE positioning, released Nov 6), and WTI managed money net length fell an eighth straight week to +21,728, about the 17th percentile of its one-year range (CFTC). December WCS is -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots, and December Houston is -$18.94 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 6), putting the export spread at +$10.73. The validated diesel crack is $91.10.
changes.conditional: An Abu Dhabi energy ceasefire, a published acceptance in the mediator process, or a settle back above $100 would each regrade the reset; a fade back toward $93 to $94 tests the week's floor a third time.
changes.delta: Friday settles: Brent Jan27 $98.32, up $0.03; WTI Dec26 $90.83, up $0.31 (Bloomberg via Rigzone). Front-month futures down about 13.2 percent on the week. Brent managed money net long 181,970, cut 63,487 in the week to Nov 3; WTI managed money net long +21,728, down 9,400, eighth straight weekly fall. December WCS -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots. December Houston -$18.94 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 6), spread +$10.73. Diesel crack $91.10 on the validated history.
changes.source: Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 6, 2026; Reuters, Nov 5-6, 2026; ICE and CFTC positioning, week ending Nov 3, 2026, released Nov 6, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 6, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Nov 7, 2026
changes.title: The weekly reset held at a $98 Brent settle, and the funds cut Brent length before Wednesday's fall, not after it

changes.balance: December stays a space and freight price, and the space leg now has the operator's own confirmation: Enbridge says the Mainline is at or near capacity and stays in apportionment for the foreseeable future. The front month itself still has not traded tighter, so the healing evidence remains entirely in the deferred tenors and in Houston.
changes.body: December WCS is -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots, a second straight zero-lot tightening, so the move is a mark, not a traded settle. The traded strip tightened for a third straight session: Jan27 -$23.85 on 1 lot, Feb27 -$23.30 on 55 lots, Apr27 -$19.35 on 275 lots, May27 -$18.30 on 275 lots and Jun27 -$17.10 on 275 lots, with Jul27 through Sep27 each on 435 lots. Houston tightened more on heavier volume: Jan27 -$16.35 on 725 lots, Feb27 -$14.90 on 685, Mar27 -$13.45 on 685, Apr27 -$12.10 on 745, May27 -$10.70 on 745, Jun27 -$9.30 on 745, and Jul27 through Sep27 flat at -$9.25 on 360 lots each. The December export spread widened to +$10.73 because both December legs are marks and Houston's mark moved further; January's spread is +$7.50.
changes.conditional: A December settle tighter on traded volume would be the first traded confirmation that the front is healing; the December apportionment notice after the Nov 17 nominations close settles the space leg against the registered call.
changes.delta: December WCS -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6), marked $0.48 tighter on zero lots, second straight zero-lot tightening. Houston Jan27 -$16.35 on 725 lots; Apr27 to Jun27 on 745 lots each. December ARV to TMW spread +$10.73, January +$7.50. December last traded wide at -$31.08 on Nov 4 (120 lots).
changes.title: December WCS marked tighter on zero lots a second day while Houston's deferred strip traded tighter on heavy volume

changes.balance: With Enbridge reported, the earnings ladder is complete and every major fall maintenance item is operator-confirmed done. The egress story into December is now the operator's standing guidance: the Mainline stays apportioned, the first optimisation barrels and the Flanagan South and Southern Access decisions sit in 2027, and Keystone's restriction lift returns space in phases rather than at once.
changes.body: Enbridge released third quarter results on Nov 6: adjusted EBITDA of C$4.434 billion, GAAP earnings of C$1.288 billion or $0.59 a share, and distributable cash flow of C$2.689 billion, with Liquids Pipelines adjusted EBITDA down $101 million on lower Line 9 tolls and reduced Flanagan South throughput. Guidance was reaffirmed at adjusted EBITDA of C$20.2 to C$20.8 billion and distributable cash flow per share of C$5.70 to C$6.10. On the call the company said the Mainline is at or near capacity and expected to remain in apportionment for the foreseeable future, with final investment decisions on the Flanagan South and Southern Access extensions expected by the next earnings date. The release carries the US$2.6 billion Tallgrass Energy crude acquisition and the sanctioned C$200 million Long Lake Expansion, in service 2028. South Bow's Keystone throughput set a quarterly record at 586 kb/d in the third quarter, with pressure restrictions lifting in phases and the Prairie Connector targeted for a mid-2027 investment decision.
changes.conditional: The December apportionment notice is the next dated egress event, after nominations close Nov 17. The Flanagan South and Southern Access decisions land by the next earnings date and are the first capacity additions the operator has dated.
changes.delta: Enbridge (Nov 6): adjusted EBITDA C$4.434 billion; guidance reaffirmed at C$20.2 to C$20.8 billion EBITDA and C$5.70 to C$6.10 distributable cash flow per share; Mainline at or near capacity and expected to remain in apportionment for the foreseeable future; Flanagan South and Southern Access final investment decisions expected by the next earnings date; Tallgrass crude acquisition US$2.6 billion; Long Lake Expansion sanctioned at C$200 million, in service 2028.
changes.source: Enbridge third quarter 2026 results and call, Nov 6, 2026; RBN Energy analyst insight, Nov 5, 2026
changes.title: Enbridge confirmed the Mainline stays in apportionment for the foreseeable future and dated its expansion decisions to the next earnings call

flags.body: Brent settled the week at $98.32 after a 13.2 percent weekly fall, recovering on a physical board that did not change: talks live and rejecting drafts, the president deciding between a deal and destruction, UKMTO incidents at October's record pace, and a fatal product tanker explosion on Nov 5. Funds cut the combined Brent and WTI net long by 78,492 contracts in the week to Nov 3, before the fall, so the flush fuel is thinner than it was. Eurasia Group prices renewed strikes at 60 percent with a $110 to $125 Brent band, a deal at 10 percent and a standoff at 30 percent. The new Congress is seated Jan 3, 2027; until then the administration's foreign policy runs under the existing composition.
flags.title: The war premium repriced and held: no deal, no accepted terms, the escalation branch priced at 60 percent, and the speculative length already cut
flags.trigger: A published agreement or acceptance in the mediator process, a confirmed strike or maritime escalation, a settle confirming or reversing the recovery, or the Abu Dhabi talks on Nov 10-11

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. The registered December judgment call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack now includes six wide or marked December settlements, a deferred strip that has tightened on traded volume for three straight sessions with Houston leading, and the operator's own statement on Nov 6 that the Mainline is at or near capacity and expected to remain in apportionment for the foreseeable future. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows the close and grades the call.
flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, the operator says apportionment persists, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop before the nominations close

flags.body: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003 and 13 percent below the five-year average, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. The validated diesel crack is $91.10, and Ukraine's refinery campaign, six plants struck since Oct 30 with Yanos halted and Saratov hit overnight into Nov 7, keeps Atlantic basin product supply under pressure while Russian product exports stay restricted. The next inventory report is Thursday Nov 12.
flags.title: Distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003: the products leg is the tight part of the US balance into winter
flags.trigger: The EIA release at 12:00 p.m. ET on Nov 12, a distillate stock build back above 105 million barrels, or a diesel crack break in either direction
